about: A record signed and sealed by name (sce:payload, docs/adr/0109, D9; docs/SCE_HOST_FEATURES.md, section 10), which
the Rust and the C++ lanes agree on byte for byte. `description` is the description of the record's type the
build writes for the note of sce-build/tests/fixtures/static_datamodel/schema_cose_note.scxml, its fields in
the order their keys encode; `record` is a note as a machine writes it, a byte string as its Latin-1 text; and
`record_cbor` is its deterministic CBOR (docs/adr/0101, section 2), which each lane's record codec writes from
`record` and reads back to it (Rust: sce_rust_runtime::record_cbor; C++: common/RecordCbor.h).
`signed` is the tagged COSE_Sign1 of `record_cbor` under the Ed25519 key whose 32-byte seed is `seed` and whose
id is the key id, with no external data; Ed25519 is deterministic, so each host's signing of the record's bytes
is this object, and each host verifies it under a trust set that holds `public_key` alone. `tampered` is
`signed` with the last byte of its signature changed, which verifies under no key. `sealed` is the tagged
COSE_Encrypt0 of `record_cbor` under the ChaCha20/Poly1305 key `key` with the nonce `nonce`, which a test
fixes. `not_a_record` holds bytes that are no value of the note, and their signed and sealed objects: an
object that verifies or opens to them is the operation's failure `not_a_record`.
Every hexadecimal value is the bytes it spells. The objects were computed by an implementation that shares
nothing with either lane (the Python `cryptography` package over OpenSSL, with a CBOR writer of its own),
which first reproduced every object of tests/host_features/cose_cross_language.json.
